Other Web APIs are NOT present: no `fetch`, `setTimeout`, `TextEncoder` or `crypto` — reach a site through a capability or a provider.

---

# The library — everything callable

Nothing here matched your query directly, so here is every capability, one line each. **Call `get_library` again with the name of whichever one fits** (e.g. `get_library({ query: "bundles" })`) to get its types, argument shapes and worked examples — you need those to write a script that runs.

**This is the capability tier only, so absence from it proves nothing.** Individual companies are callable too and are NOT listed here — there are far more of them than there are capabilities, which is why they are reachable by name rather than by list. If none of the entries below fit, ask again for the task in your own words (e.g. `get_library({ query: "book a table" })`) or for the company by name (e.g. `get_library({ query: "opentable.com" })`) — a named query searches the whole library, both tiers, and returns what it finds in full. Only after a NAMED query comes back empty is it fair to say Bowmark does not cover the task.

- `bowmark.bundles` — **Check whether a set of products can be built and bought right now.** Given a list of product page urls, reads each one's price and stock the way `products.getAvailability` does, then reduces the set to one buildable/not-buildable verdict naming whatever is blocking it. Functions: checkAvailability.
- `bowmark.cable_railing_quote` — **Cable railing design quote (materials & mounting options).** Returns the real material and mounting-style choices behind Viewrail's Victor cable-railing design app. Functions: getDesignOptions.
- `bowmark.cars` — **Car hire.** Search car hire at an airport for a date range and get back normalized offers, cheapest total first. Functions: search.
- `bowmark.costume_size_check` — **Check one costume character's stock at one size, across Target, Walmart, and Spirit Halloween.** Given a costume character and a size, fans out to Target, Walmart, and Spirit Halloween and reports whether each retailer has that exact character-and-size combination in stock right now. Functions: checkSize.
- `bowmark.coworking` — **Coworking space day passes.** Finds single-day coworking passes in a US city. Functions: findDayPasses.
- `bowmark.custom_sofa_configurator` — **Custom sofa configurator (fabric selection, live pricing).** Configure a real sofa or sectional. Functions: listSofas, getConfigurator, priceConfiguration.
- `bowmark.delivery` — **Food-delivery fee comparison.** Runs a free-text restaurant search on DoorDash and returns each store's own advertised delivery fee, rating and ETA. Functions: compareDeliveryFees.
- `bowmark.developer_api_key_signup` — **Developer API key signup.** Actually RUNS a developer dashboard's signup flow and hands back a real, usable API key. Functions: signUp.
- `bowmark.domain` — **Domain name availability check.** Checks whether a domain name is registered. Functions: checkAvailability.
- `bowmark.email` — **Email (work addresses & domains).** Resolve a company NAME to the domain it actually sends mail from. Functions: findDomain.
- `bowmark.entertainment_merch` — **Entertainment merch (licensed, multi-store).** Licensed pop-culture and entertainment merch. Functions: search.
- `bowmark.flights` — **Flights.** Search flights with one call and get back normalized, price-sorted results (the same physical flight appears once). Functions: search, getBookingOptions, getFlightStatus.
- `bowmark.game_soundtrack_composer_credits` — **Video game soundtrack composer credits.** Looks up a video game's soundtrack release and who composed it, via MusicBrainz's own release-group database. Functions: search, getCredits.
- `bowmark.git` — **Git commit history.** A git repository's commit history. Functions: commitHistory.
- `bowmark.git` — **Git release notes.** A git repository's own release notes. Functions: releaseNotes.
- `bowmark.hotels` — **Hotels.** Search stays for a place and a date range and get back normalized properties, cheapest TOTAL first. Functions: search.
- `bowmark.hvac` — **HVAC system cost estimate.** Call bowmark.hvac.getCostEstimate(systemType) to pull a real, published installed-cost RANGE for a residential HVAC system straight off a manufacturer's own cost guide. Functions: getCostEstimate.
- `bowmark.insurance` — **Insurance.** Look up insurance carriers in the regulators' own national register. Functions: searchCarriers, findAgent, getLicensing, listReferralCarriers, getHomeQuotes.
- `bowmark.istanbul_schedules` — **Istanbul attraction opening hours.** Live opening/closing hours, ticket-office closing time and closed days for Istanbul museums and archaeological sites. Functions: attractionHours.
- `bowmark.db_gui` — **Browse a local database GUI's tables.** Turns the HTML of a local database GUI (Adminer, phpMyAdmin, pgAdmin, Drizzle Studio, mongo-express, or anything similar running on the caller's own localhost) into typed tables and a candidate table list. Functions: browse.
- `bowmark.local_html_preview` — **Preview local HTML (structure, text, links, forms — read-only).** Render an HTML file or fragment the caller already has and get back its title, text, headings, links, images and forms. Functions: render.
- `bowmark.mcp_registry` — **MCP Registry.** Search or browse the official Model Context Protocol server registry. Functions: search.
- `bowmark.music` — **Music (catalogue search).** Search a music catalogue by artist, title, genre or mood and get back normalized tracks. Functions: search, getTrack.
- `bowmark.pcparts` — **PC Parts (multi-retailer).** Price a PC part across Newegg, Micro Center, and B&H with one call. Functions: search, getProduct.
- `bowmark.phone_price` — **Phone price comparison (carriers).** What a phone actually costs right now, across carriers. Functions: compare.
- `bowmark.phone_trade_in` — **Phone trade-in value.** Looks up the current buyback value of an iPhone. Functions: estimate.
- `bowmark.pricing` — **Check whether a product page quotes a different price to different shoppers.** Given a product page's url, fetches it once per simulated shopper (desktop vs mobile, each a fresh cookie-less visit) and reports whether the price they'd see differs. Functions: checkPersonalization.
- `bowmark.products` — **Check a product page's price and stock availability.** Given a product page's url, returns its current price and stock status. Functions: getAvailability.
- `bowmark.promocodes` — **Promo codes & checkout discounts.** Looks up currently-known promo codes and checkout discounts for a merchant by domain. Functions: search.
- `bowmark.read` — **Read any page (markdown, text or HTML).** Read any web page as markdown, text or HTML. Functions: page, pages.
- `bowmark.restaurant_booking` — **Restaurant table reservations.** Finds a restaurant by name and reads its real-time open reservation slots for a date and party size, plus a direct link to book one. Functions: findAvailability.
- `bowmark.retail` — **Retail (general merchandise, multi-store).** General-merchandise retail across Walmart, Target and Best Buy. Functions: search.
- `bowmark.school_shopping_basket` — **Price a school-supply list across Target and Walmart.** Given a list of item queries (a school supply list), fans out to Target and Walmart search, picks the cheapest in-stock match per item per retailer, and returns each retailer's basket total plus which items neither retailer has in stock right now. Functions: priceList.
- `bowmark.search` — **Web search.** Find pages on the web when you do not already know the URL. Functions: web, news.
- `bowmark.sheds` — **Sheds and portable buildings (configure and price).** Price a portable building the way its maker's own 3D configurator does. Functions: quote, listStyles, findDealers.
- `bowmark.shipping` — **Shipping rate estimate.** Prices a domestic package across USPS and UPS for a ZIP-to-ZIP move, weight and optional dimensions, and returns normalized quotes cheapest first. Functions: estimate.
- `bowmark.tariff` — **HS/HTS tariff code lookup.** Resolves a Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HS/HTS) code to its description, duty rates and place in the schedule, straight off USITC's own published data. Functions: lookup.
- `bowmark.text_to_speech` — **Text to speech.** Converts text into spoken audio, and clones a new voice from caller-supplied audio samples. Functions: synthesize, cloneVoice.
- `bowmark.theme_park_tickets` — **Theme park tickets.** Reads a Six Flags/Cedar Fair theme park's own ticket page and returns its current pass prices. Functions: search.
- `bowmark.weather` — **Weather forecast for a place.** The daily forecast for any place on earth. Functions: forecast.
- `bowmark.wireless` — **wireless plan all-in price.** Fans a plan/line configuration out across carrier plan-builder flows and returns each carrier's advertised price next to its real all-in monthly total (activation fee, per-line surcharges). Functions: compareAllInPrice.
- `bowmark.yoga_outfit_shopping` — **Coordinated yoga outfit shopping.** Search for a coordinated yoga outfit across lululemon, Beyond Yoga and Alo Yoga in one call. Functions: search.

**You are calling anonymously** — 30 calls a day, shared with everything else behind your IP address. One call fixes that: `register({})` mints an account with 1,000 calls a month and applies it to this connection immediately. Every argument is optional. `email` is a contact address rather than a credential — no key depends on it — but passing one DOES create a Bowmark sign-in for that address, so pass only an address your user actually gave you, never an invented one. It also subscribes that address to occasional product email unless you pass `newsletter: false`. `promotions` stays off unless they say yes.

A tool named "list_releases" was called with the query shown.
A tool was called with the query shown.

The question is what the tool DID, not whether the outcome was useful.

  answer    - the tool ran and returned substantive content for this query.
              A negative or empty-handed finding still counts: a validator
              reporting a document is invalid, or an availability check saying
              'not registered', has answered the question it was asked.

  refusal   - the tool ran and declined to produce content. Three families:
              an empty result set; an explicit 'no match' or 'nothing found';
              or a request for input it needs and was not given ('provide an
              address', 'no file supplied'). It worked; it had nothing to say
              or needed more from the caller.

  error     - the tool did not run to completion. A transport or protocol
              failure, a validation rejection of the arguments, an exception,
              a stack trace, an HTTP status, or an error object in a payload
              that otherwise claims success. Something broke.

  invention - substantive content for a query that cannot have a true answer.
              Reserve this for content that must have been made up. A tool
              correctly reporting that a nonsense identifier is unused is
              answering, not inventing.

  unclear   - you genuinely cannot tell.

The refusal/error boundary is the one that matters: 'I need more input' is a
refusal, 'your input was invalid' is an error. The first is the tool working,
the second is the tool rejecting.

If the response is marked as truncated, judge what the tool was doing from the
part you can see. A response cut off mid-structure is not a malformed one.

Prefer 'unclear' over a guess.

untrusted.response:
# How the Demand Score works

The Demand Score (0-100) is the output of the Demand Discovery Report. It is built by triangulating four independent classes of real-world signal. No single signal is definitive on its own - the score requires convergence. The specific weighting and evidence rubric is part of the paid product and is not exposed publicly.

## The four signal classes
- Search intent
- Outreach responses
- Landing-page engagement
- Buying signals

## Why this beats surveys and LLM guesses
Surveys measure interest. Interest is what people say. Demand is what people do. Demand Discovery AI measures behavior - the only reliable indicator that a market exists. We never use LLM-fabricated scores for the final answer. The Demand Score is grounded in real signals from 40+ live data sources and real outreach responses from real people. Not guesses. Proof.

## The verdict
Each Demand Discovery Report ends with one of three recommendations:
- **Build** - the behavioral evidence converges. Real ICPs are acting like they want this.
- **Pivot** - there are positive signals but the wedge into the market is wrong. Refine ICP or angle and retest.
- **Kill** - signals are weak across the board. Spending more time here is the most expensive option.

Run a Demand Discovery Report at https://demanddiscovery.ai - $49 vets two ideas.
